keyFindings.description: A reloaded comment edit's Retry gets 422 KEY_REUSED. The first save sends {body, blocks, base_revision} under key K, and sendAttempt builds that body once. After a reload past KEPT_SEND_RESUME_MS, the write reads as refused with SendInterruptedError, and `restore` rebuilds the edit with `blocks: undefined`. A Retry with an unchanged draft goes under the same key K (requestFor → retriesUnderItsKey, since SendInterruptedError is a SendStoppedError), but HeldSends.send builds a fresh sendAttempt whose PATCH has no blocks or base_revision. The server judges a key by the body's digest (request_keys.go) and answers 422 KEY_REUSED, even when the first save landed. On main the restored edit sent the same {body}, so this came with the merge. Fix: keep the press-time carried ids in KeptComposerSend.edit and send them on restore, or make a Retry under its own key reuse the kept wire request. Add a reload-then-Retry edit case to held-sends.test.ts.

A replayed keyed message write answers reply_block null. recoveredMessage reads the message with loadMessage (scanMessage only) and never calls hydrateMessageReplyBlocks. replayIssueMessage and replayAgentMessage answer from it, and writeRefreshed keeps only advice and ask_waiting_on from the stored answer. So a repeat of a committed keyed POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/messages or /agents/{session_id}/messages, for a reply that names a block, says it answers the whole message. That breaks the PR's rule that every message a route returns carries reply_block. Comments are fine: replayComment goes through hydrateCommentSideTables. Fix: hydrateMessageReplyBlocks in recoveredMessage, plus a replay test for a reply that names a block.
